answer: Trust-flow capping resists sybils: an agent's weight is the trust that can travel from long-standing seed nodes along vouch edges, and every edge has a fixed capacity. A thousand fake accounts vouching for each other add no extra signal because they touch honest agents only through a few attack edges. Picture a comet with a huge bright tail of fakes, all hanging by one thin thread of capacity; buying more weight means winning real vouches, so cost tracks the cut, not the account count.
